answer: One ridge wildlife census post per applicant for 120 days. A 150 token deposit and a 100 dollar license open it, and each daily page carries an onyx seal. The keeper photographs every falcon sighted, notes its time and direction, and logs the noon zenith reading. A ranger visits twice to check the log against weather notes and neighbor counts. A forged page forfeits the deposit and bars the keeper 180 days. Faking 10,000 posts freezes 1,500,000 tokens and costs 1,000,000 dollars in fees. A fake census is like a forged tide table: high water exposes it, and the keeper loses the post.
